rules.providerOnboarding: No provider with a publicly stated KYB/KYC requirement. Exception: dRPC under Opsis decision D20, admitted only while it does not request identity or business verification.

admittedPaidProviders.purpose: Production JSON-RPC reads for Robinhood Chain 4663
admittedPaidProviders.billing: Founder-funded prepaid cryptocurrency balance; no card-billed pay-as-you-go or automatic upgrade
admittedPaidProviders.applicationFuse: DRPC_MONTHLY_CU_LIMIT, default 166000000 compute units per UTC month, fail-closed

rules.branchCreation: Registered queued releases may be prepared on private branches. Only the active release may ship; integrate current main and reverify before activation.
rules.staging: Gate-passed private previews must be isolated and access-restricted. Production-connected staging services must not be repurposed for unfinished work.

releases.outcome: Preview a live swap
releases.shipGate: Fresh Uniswap quote and successful simulation; all user-paid costs are disclosed; official-app handoff requotes; no signing method exists.

releases.outcome: Use Opsis without becoming a profile
releases.shipGate: Private Mode needs no account; browser tokens are not readable by JavaScript; private fields never enter logs, analytics, or saved server records; legacy cloud data can be exported and deleted.

releases.outcome: Track every asset privately
releases.shipGate: Lots, notes, photos, and purchase prices are encrypted in IndexedDB with tested export, import, lock, recovery, deletion, and storage-eviction states; plaintext never crosses the network.

releases.outcome: See holdings, performance, activity, and risk together
releases.shipGate: Balances, NFTs, transactions, approvals, and decoded movements reconcile against one captured current block whose hash is rechecked; the non-final anchor and bounded coverage are explicit; manual lot math is deterministic; saved ownership context remains encrypted and browser-local.

releases.outcome: Understand tokenized assets, yield, and physical claims
releases.shipGate: Stock Token identity, multipliers, corporate actions, oracle freshness, Morpho vault state, custody claims, and redemption limits are source-linked; unsupported authenticity is never inferred.

releases.outcome: Add cards and collectibles without a spreadsheet
releases.shipGate: A field-selective TCGdex GraphQL request resolves English card ID, set, collector number, category, rarity, and illustrator without requesting artwork, marketplace pricing, or printing metadata. Owner-supplied printing or variant, condition, grade, certificate, locally sanitized photo, and dated manual value source are explicitly labeled and encrypted locally; none is treated as provider-verified authenticity, current market data, or inventory. Manual assets remain usable without a match or provider.

releases.outcome: Compare fresh liquidity, prices, stock, and available product/source signals
releases.shipGate: Exact-match confidence, source freshness, landed-cost inputs, inventory state, and provider-reported product signals are visible; missing seller reputation is explicit and unsupported venues use precise search handoffs instead of scraping.

releases.outcome: Rebuild a trade or purchase safely
releases.shipGate: Historical calldata and checkout data are never reused; users choose a new amount or offer; official Uniswap or merchant checkout independently requotes and owns execution.

releases.outcome: Reuse Opsis's reviewed public support data
releases.shipGate: The capped API exposes a two-entry reviewed static support registry plus independently derived syntax normalization; it contains no Vault data or restricted upstream payloads and cannot create paid overage.

releases.outcome: Certify the enabled private asset command center for launch
releases.shipGate: End-to-end launch journeys pass on desktop and mobile; dependency, privacy, accessibility, provider-failure, load, legal-copy, backup, deletion, monitoring, and rollback gates are complete.

releases.outcome: Understand discovered spending permissions and prepare a safe external revocation
releases.shipGate: Current ERC20, ERC721 and operator permissions are anchored, source-linked and explicitly bounded by discovery coverage; revoked, unknown and unavailable are distinct; no safety verdict or exhaustive scan is implied. External revocation requires a verified chain-supported destination, explicit disclosure of network costs and user-controlled execution; Opsis never signs or broadcasts.

releases.outcome: Compare private trade scenarios and their portfolio effects without executing
releases.shipGate: Fresh supported quotes drive exact before/after quantities, allocation assumptions and disclosed costs; stale, unsupported, insufficient-balance and failed-quote states are tested. Saved scenarios are encrypted locally. Quote previews are not described as guaranteed execution or full transaction simulation; official tools independently requote and own execution.

releases.currentSlice: Card Price Check: standalone public reference prices only. Automatic live offers and sold-listing aggregation remain access-restricted and unshipped; the listing ship gate below is not claimed complete.
releases.outcome: Check source-linked collectible reference prices without confusing references with live offers
releases.shipGate: The shipped Card Price Check slice keeps exact card identity, timestamps, currencies and source links visible; stale, missing and failed prices remain explicit. Optional artwork is click-only. Reference prices are not appraisals, available inventory or executable offers. English/Chinese and desktop/mobile checks pass; automatic offer aggregation remains disabled.
releases.deferredScope: Automatic offers and sold-listing aggregation remain unshipped and access-restricted. Advancing Watch does not enable or certify them.
releases.deferredShipGate: Supported authorized free-tier sources distinguish printing, condition and grade, list known landed costs and timestamp every offer. Sold-price evidence is independently labeled and never fabricated; unknown shipping and weak matches cannot rank as guaranteed cheapest. Provider limits fail closed without overage; unsupported venues use explicit search handoffs rather than claimed live listings.

releases.outcome: Save wallets privately and see what changed between checks
releases.shipGate: Wallet labels and bounded snapshot history are encrypted locally. User-triggered public-address refreshes show exact comparable balance changes and newly observed activity with block anchors, source links and coverage gaps; missing is never zero, transfers are not inferred trades, and no background monitoring or profit claims are made. Persistence, backup/restore, deletion, stale/reorg/provider errors, concurrency, accessibility and English/Chinese mobile flows are tested. No signing, new provider, recurring vendor cost or private-data upload is introduced.

releases.outcome: Explore source-linked world events and observed crypto prices around publication
releases.shipGate: Preserve the current shared shell and shipped routes. Verify exact publication-aligned samples, missing-data gaps, dated capture and prepared AI context, real photo/source credits, keyboard controls, modal focus, mobile layouts, WebGL fallback and default-off behavior. No continuous-feed claims, causal attribution, transactions, new paid providers or incremental recurring vendor spend.

releases.outcome: Review saved activity across watched wallets in one private feed
releases.shipGate: Bounded retained snapshots produce a deduplicated, source-linked local feed. Wallet and asset filters send no network requests. Baseline activity, later discoveries, failed transactions, incomplete movements and conflicting observations remain distinct. Locked and disabled states expose no private data; persistence, English/Chinese, mobile and browser tests pass. No polling, new providers or storage migration.

releases.outcome: Compare exact token holdings shared by selected watched wallets
releases.shipGate: Local latest snapshots group positive ERC20 holdings by exact chain and contract, never symbol. Different capture times, partial coverage, incompatible decimals and unavailable prior holdings remain visible. Per-wallet exact changes never imply buys, identity, coordination or profit. Disabled/locked, selection, precision, persistence, Chinese and mobile tests pass.

releases.outcome: Try a portfolio shock instantly and understand concentration without connecting a wallet
releases.shipGate: Clearly hypothetical presets and editable USD reference values drive exact local-only single-position and all-position scenarios. Concentration is not a correlation or safety rating. Accessible responsive visuals, English/Chinese, invalid inputs, default-off routing and privacy-safe previewed image export pass automated browser and unit tests. No provider, storage migration, account, signing or recurring spend.

releases.outcome: Inspect original KOL posts, compare stated targets and curate a private source watchlist
releases.shipGate: Real profile images and original post links retain provenance. Dated selected coverage, conditional forecasts, opinions, holdings and unavailable outcomes remain distinct. Filters, saved receipts, comparison, source explanations, mobile and disabled states are tested. No invented accuracy, performance, wallet attribution, live coverage, new paid provider, external execution or recurring spend.

releases.outcome: Compare current and proposed allocations under explicit hypothetical per-position shocks
releases.shipGate: Exact local cents math, same-total fair comparisons, input validation, local selected Vault value import with missing/date/currency boundaries, responsive English/Chinese, keyboard, lock cleanup, no private uploads, providers, predictions or trading.

releases.outcome: Understand material changes across watched wallets since comparable saved checks
releases.shipGate: Bounded deterministic local briefing from retained snapshots, evidence links, baseline/gaps/reorg/failure states explicit; no buy/sell inference, background monitoring or new providers; locked/disabled/privacy and English/Chinese/mobile tests.

releases.outcome: Get question-specific wallet, transaction and token answers with clear evidence and relevant next actions
releases.shipGate: Deterministic factual task-specific presentation, uncertainty visible when material, no invented safety/identity/holdings, sources and private persistence preserved, optional English/Chinese goals tested and no new providers.

releases.outcome: Show a compact captured Coinbase ETH/USD market brief in Situation Room
releases.shipGate: Contextualized static single-venue Coinbase ETH/USD snapshot only; explicit captured/not-live/stale states; complete hourly candles with disclosed gaps and strict HTTPS/no-credential source validation; source-linked dated macro context without causal claims; and a stress-test hypothesis handoff. No new providers, polling, or invented reference venues.

releases.outcome: Follow a verified public wallet into Watch from any result that shows one
releases.shipGate: One reusable chain-aware follow action appears only for a supported-chain public address that is not the zero, dead or a classified-contract address; unknown classification is labelled a public address, never an EOA or proven wallet. The action links to Watch carrying the public address only, pre-fills it without automatic consent, lookup or save, and guides locked/create/unlocked states without losing the address. Encrypted Vault labels never enter a URL. Wallet-result, transaction-participant, invalid/zero/dead/contract, feature-disabled and locked/unlocked flows are tested with no new provider, key, signing, payment or recurring spend.

releases.outcome: See whether an observed position could realistically be exited and what it would cost
releases.shipGate: One fresh read-only exit estimate per request from the official Uniswap V3 factory and QuoterV2 on chain 4663. Only factory-verified standard fee-tier pools are quoted; the best successful pool is selected, arbitrary V3 tokens require validated on-chain decimals, and v4-only or unknown-decimal tokens fail closed as unsupported. A captured latest block is rechecked by hash; stale, reorged, rate-limited, malformed and over-budget states fail closed within a reviewed low RPC cap with no aggressive retry. Fee and price impact use exact BigInt math against the same-block pool spot quote, coverage lists tested/quoted/missing/failed pools, and active V3 liquidity is shown only as a raw parameter that is not cash capacity or a safety verdict. A quote is explicitly not proof of transferability, sellability, or guaranteed execution. Default-off API and web flags, English/Chinese, desktop/mobile, no signing or broadcast, no new provider, paid path, account or recurring spend.

releases.outcome: Compare the largest observed trades for a token or wallet and follow the public addresses involved
releases.shipGate: Largest observed amounts come from bounded, timestamped, source-linked decoded Uniswap V3 Swap logs with signed amount0/amount1 for explicit pools and an explicit block window, not from raw ERC-20 transfer records. Matched-log caps, partial coverage, missing or out-of-window records, failed transactions and unknown counterparties remain distinct; ranking never infers buys, sells, identity, coordination or profit. Public participant addresses reuse the release 23 chain-aware follow action with no automatic lookup or save, and ranking is deterministic, excluding zero, dead and classified-contract addresses. Locked/disabled ownership, English/Chinese and mobile are tested; no signing or polling. Production reads use only the D20 dRPC transport, behind its fail-closed monthly fuse; no other new provider or recurring spend.

releases.outcome: Build the Opsis four-workspace specification in reviewed batches, integrating existing research, exact-size trade checks, private Watch and reproducible local Quant experiments
releases.shipGate: Default-off Opsis preparation within the existing four workspaces; D13 permits the isolated public preview after verification. Relevant unit, numerical, failure-state, privacy, English/Chinese, Chromium/WebKit and full release gates must pass on the integrated candidate. Same-block bounded exit ladders preserve exact math and quotas. Watch conditions and inbox state remain encrypted locally and never imply continuous monitoring. Quant imports and seeded experiments run locally with eligibility checks, cancellation, provenance and reproducible manifests. New capture sources, chains, paid AI or execution stay disabled pending their separate admission and decision gates. No provider, execution, chain, paid path or frozen /quant change is admitted by this release. The active release and production order remain unchanged.

releases.outcome: Move through Opsis without dead ends, lost results, mismatched names or laggy clicks
releases.shipGate: One name per destination across the front door, navigation, guide, titles and copy in English and Chinese. No link or shortcut reaches a switched-off tool. The front door keeps its D12 composition while every shortcut opens its tool with one consistent transition and controls respond once visible. Public context lives in the URL and survives back, refresh and returning within a tab; private Vault data never enters a URL. Clicks show progress at once with no blank full-screen loader after first load. The tool input sits on the first screen at 375 px. Privacy and Terms render in the shared shell with no broken links. Localized titles, a whole-page persisted theme and a constant header height. No provider, chain, execution, paid path, workspace or frozen /quant change. Relevant unit, failure-state, privacy, English/Chinese, Chromium/WebKit and full release gates pass on the integrated candidate.

releases.outcome: Opsis is the only product name in the product, code, configuration and documentation
releases.shipGate: No mention of the predecessor product, its tool brands or earlier working names in user-visible copy (English and Chinese), metadata, emails, API responses, code identifiers, configuration, scripts or documentation, except the documented compatibility identifiers that existing users' saved data, backups and cookies still need. Existing encrypted Vault data, backups, exports, cookies and saved reports keep working: new data uses the Opsis identifiers and old identifiers are still read. Web and API stay compatible in either deployment order. On-chain token symbols and third-party names are unchanged. No provider, chain, execution, paid path or workspace change; the frozen /quant page changes only its product name. Relevant unit, failure-state, privacy, English/Chinese, Chromium/WebKit and full release gates pass on the integrated candidate.

releases.outcome: Model what a perp position costs to hold and where it would be liquidated, then take the scenario to a venue that accepts you
releases.shipGate: The local Perp cost scenario adds funding over a holding period, an estimated liquidation price for an isolated linear position and a side-by-side comparison, all from user-entered inputs with exact decimal arithmetic, stated assumptions and refusal on insufficient or invalid input; nothing is fetched from a venue. A reviewed, dated venue directory lists only venues whose own published pages say they offer perpetual futures in the user's stated region (United States, Canada or elsewhere), with conditions, sources and review date; it marks itself as needing re-review after 120 days and is controlled by a server flag that defaults off on API and web. Opsis places, routes, transmits and receives no order, verifies no identity or eligibility, ranks no venue, carries no referral parameter and suggests no workaround; the stated region never leaves the browser and perpExecution stays false. The API stops accepting the earlier request header. English and Chinese, 320 px to desktop, Chromium and WebKit, unit, failure-state, privacy and full release gates pass on the integrated candidate. No provider, chain, execution, paid path or new workspace.

releases.outcome: Publishing the final domain and the support address is a settings change, and the site carries the files a public launch expects
releases.shipGate: A support and security contact address supplied at build time appears on the Privacy page in English and Chinese and in /.well-known/security.txt; with no address configured the current sentence stays and no security file is written; a malformed address fails the build. Search indexing stays off by default, with every Opsis page marked noindex as today; an explicit build switch on an HTTPS site origin writes sitemap.xml and the Sitemap line in robots.txt from the canonical site URL and lets only the always-available public pages be indexed. The site ships a favicon and a touch icon. The API accepts state-changing requests from its canonical origin and from explicitly configured alias origins only, each a canonical HTTPS origin, so the earlier host keeps working during a domain move; the default is no alias and nothing else about the request checks changes. The in-app changelog gains the release 29 entry in the wording approved by D23. A runbook covers the domain move, the contact address, verification and rollback. No provider, chain, execution, paid path, workspace, public claim or invariant change. Relevant unit, failure-state, privacy, English/Chinese, Chromium/WebKit and full release gates pass on the integrated candidate.

releases.outcome: A first-time visitor gets a useful answer from the first thing they try
releases.shipGate: Research recognises a token contract without being told and shows its name, symbol, decimals and supply with the exact contract; a transaction shows decoded token transfers, approvals and Uniswap V3 swaps in plain words with formatted amounts next to the raw values, and says so when it could not decode; a wallet shows its sampled token balances in the result. Decoding uses only the existing chain-data provider within the existing per-request and daily limits, and anything not established stays labelled as unknown. Trade Check never preselects the input token as its output and explains a refused request specifically. Research and Trade Check offer one-click examples that use public reviewed contracts only, never an individual's wallet, and accept the symbols of reviewed assets while always showing the exact contract they resolve to. On Research and Trade Check the main input and its action are on the first screen at 1280 by 800 and 375 by 812, with one header height across tool pages. English and Chinese, Chromium and WebKit, unit, failure-state, privacy and full release gates pass on the integrated candidate. No provider, chain, execution, paid path, workspace or new public claim; the front door keeps its D12 composition.
